description: Two islands whose outward rings meet in the narrow channel between them. Because rings are derived from the UNION of all land (S10) then clipped to water (S11/S14), the overlapping bands must merge into ONE clean shared band with no pinch and no double coverage — never two colliding ring sets. This is the single test that proves the signature coastal-ring effect is correct.
geometry_notes: Island edges face each other at x=450 (A) and x=550 (B): a 100px channel.
4 rings * 14px = 56px reach from each coast; 56+56=112 > 100, so the grown regions OVERLAP across the channel and MUST union into a shared band.
channel bbox below stays inside the channel (x 455..545) and off both islands.

assertions.note: The bands in the channel are ONE connected component — no pinch, no two separate ring sets.
Coverage multiplicity <= 1: the merged band never double-stacks where the two islands' offsets overlap.
No ring band covers either island's interior.
The channel midpoint IS covered by a ring band (the shared band fills the strait).
The center of island A is land, not ring.
Just off A's west coast (edge x=290, ~20px out) is covered by rings.
Far open sea >56px west of A's coast (edge x=290, reach to x=234) is NOT covered.
